premises.title: Equal liberties and democratic standing
premises.text: An admissible regime is feasible, respects equal fundamental liberties and permits effective democratic control. Ownership, employment and cognitive ability do not determine civic standing.

premises.title: Priority to the least advantaged
premises.text: A just regime is admissible and maximizes Q, the lowest needs-adjusted access, among admissible regimes. This is a normative choice; existence of a maximum is not assumed.

premises.title: A sufficient admissible alternative
premises.text: There is a feasible alternative that respects the same liberties and democratic requirements and covers every person’s essential needs.

premises.title: Actual essential deprivation
premises.text: At least one person receives less than their essential-needs threshold in the regime under examination.

premises.title: Strict institutional superiority
premises.text: A specified admissible regime has a strictly higher Q than every other admissible regime. This performance hypothesis must be established independently.

premises.title: Rising capital income, fixed ownership
premises.text: Capital income rises between two periods, ownership shares stay fixed and there is no collective redistribution. Quantities represent real access, including price effects.

premises.title: Fixed output and divisible resources
premises.text: The population is finite and nonempty, needs are positive, total access is bounded by Y and proportional allocations are feasible without changing output.

premises.title: Equal labor income and a nonowner
premises.text: Compare a nonowner in a private regime with equal labor incomes and a collective regime with equal allocations. Population and private output are positive; needs are identical for the needs comparison.

premises.title: An effective binary majority vote
premises.text: Equal valid ballots exhaust the electorate; more than half support the alternative. Free informed preferences, admissible options and implementation of the result are institutional assumptions.

premises.title: Sustainable collective innovation
premises.text: A regime sustains innovation without concentrated private capital, including maintenance, renewal and necessary human work.

premises.title: Every regime can be improved
premises.text: For every admissible regime there is another admissible regime with strictly higher Q. This is a separate scenario, not a claim about the present economy.

results.title: Reading the needs threshold
results.text: All essential needs are covered exactly when Q is at least one. The minimum is witnessed in the model.
steps: A witnessed minimum identifies one person at Q. Positive needs allow cancellation of their needs coefficient.
Conversely, Q ≥ 1 and the lower-bound property give cᵢ ≥ bᵢ for every person.
results.limit: Exact rational model; needs, access and the minimum must have their stated meaning.

proof.code:
theorem universal_needs_iff_floor {P R : Type} (m : Model P R) (r : R) :
    UniversalNeeds m r ↔ 1 ≤ m.floor r := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := m.floor_attained r
    have hni := h i
    have hm : 1 * m.needs i ≤ m.floor r * m.needs i := by grind
    exact Rat.le_of_mul_le_mul_right hm (m.needs_pos i)
  · intro h i
    have hm := Rat.mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right h (show 0 ≤ m.needs i by
      have := m.needs_pos i; grind)
    have hl := m.floor_lower r i
    grind

results.title: Justice includes admissibility
results.text: A just regime must be feasible and satisfy the stipulated liberty and democracy requirements.
steps: Extract the admissibility component from the definition of justice.
results.limit: A definitional consequence. Lean does not certify that a real institution is democratic.

proof.code:
theorem just_is_admissible {P R : Type} (m : Model P R) (r : R)
    (justice : Just m r) : Admissible m r := justice.1

results.title: Avoidable deprivation is excluded
results.text: If a sufficient admissible alternative exists, every just regime covers everyone’s essential needs. A separate no-deprivation axiom is unnecessary.
steps: The sufficient alternative has Q(s) ≥ 1.
Maximin justice gives Q(r) ≥ Q(s), hence Q(r) ≥ 1.
results.limit: The alternative must satisfy the same liberties and democratic requirements. The proof does not establish that it exists.

proof.code:
theorem needs_from_maximin {P R : Type} (m : Model P R) (r s : R)
    (justice : Just m r) (alternative : Admissible m s)
    (sufficient : UniversalNeeds m s) : UniversalNeeds m r := by
  have hs := (universal_needs_iff_floor m s).mp sufficient
  have hr := justice.2 s alternative
  apply (universal_needs_iff_floor m r).mpr
  grind

results.title: Exclusion despite feasible sufficiency is unjust
results.text: A regime with essential deprivation is not just if an admissible alternative covers everyone’s needs. This applies even if the deprived group is a minority.
results.formula: Admissible(s) ∧ Q(s) ≥ 1 ∧ (∃ i, cᵢ(r) < bᵢ) ⇒ ¬ Just(r)
steps: Assuming justice would imply universal needs coverage by the preceding theorem.
The deprived person contradicts that coverage.
results.limit: Injustice is relative to the declared principles, not a theorem that every form of capitalism is impossible.

proof.code:
theorem avoidable_deprivation_not_just {P R : Type} (m : Model P R) (r s : R)
    (alternative : Admissible m s) (sufficient : UniversalNeeds m s)
    (deprivation : ∃ i, m.access r i < m.needs i) : ¬ Just m r := by
  intro justice
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := deprivation
  have hn := needs_from_maximin m r s justice alternative sufficient i
  grind

results.title: When one institution is uniquely just
results.text: A strictly best admissible regime is just, and every just regime equals it. A collective regime qualifies only if its strict superiority is independently established.
results.formula: Admissible(s) ∧ (∀ r ≠ s, Admissible(r) ⇒ Q(r) < Q(s)) ⇒ Just(s) ∧ (Just(r) ⇒ r = s)
steps: Strict superiority implies that the candidate maximizes Q.
Another just regime would have Q at least as high, contradicting strict superiority.
results.limit: No economic system is assumed to meet this demanding performance condition.

proof.code:
theorem unique_best_is_unique_just {P R : Type} (m : Model P R) (best : R)
    (admissible : Admissible m best)
    (strict : ∀ r, Admissible m r → r ≠ best → m.floor r < m.floor best) :
    Just m best ∧ ∀ r, Just m r → r = best := by
  classical
  constructor
  · refine ⟨admissible, ?_⟩
    intro r hr
    by_cases same : r = best
    · subst r; grind
    · have := strict r hr same; grind
  · intro r hr
    apply Classical.byContradiction
    intro different
    have hlt := strict r hr.1 different
    have hle := hr.2 best admissible
    grind

results.title: A maximum need not exist
results.text: If every admissible regime has a strictly better admissible alternative, no regime satisfies exact maximin justice.
results.formula: (∀ r ∈ A, ∃ s ∈ A, Q(r) < Q(s)) ⇒ ¬ ∃ r, Just(r)
steps: Assume a just regime and select its strictly better admissible alternative.
The improvement contradicts maximization.
results.limit: This concerns exact optimization. It does not exclude approximate justice or finite comparisons.

proof.code:
theorem no_maximum_no_just {P R : Type} (m : Model P R)
    (improvement : ∀ r, Admissible m r →
      ∃ s, Admissible m s ∧ m.floor r < m.floor s) :
    ¬ ∃ r, Just m r := by
  rintro ⟨r, hr⟩
  obtain ⟨s, hs, better⟩ := improvement r hr.1
  exact strictly_better_rules_out_justice m r s hs better hr

results.title: Separate labor and capital gains
results.text: With fixed ownership and zero redistribution, the change in real access equals the change in labor income plus the owned share of the change in capital income.
steps: Expand the income formula at both dates and subtract.
results.limit: An identity under fixed shares and zero redistribution, not an empirical wage forecast.

proof.code:
theorem income_change_identity (l0 l1 share p0 p1 n : Rat) :
    income l1 share p1 0 n - income l0 share p0 0 n =
      (l1 - l0) + share * (p1 - p0) := by
  unfold income
  grind

results.title: The exact individual loss condition
results.text: When capital income increases, a person loses real access exactly when their ownership share is below the threshold compensating their lost labor income.
steps: Rearrange the income inequality.
Divide by the positive increase in capital income.
results.limit: A majority loses only if this inequality holds for more than half the population. Concentration alone is insufficient.

proof.code:
theorem loss_threshold (l0 l1 share p0 p1 n : Rat) (growth : 0 < p1 - p0) :
    income l1 share p1 0 n < income l0 share p0 0 n ↔
      share < (l0 - l1) / (p1 - p0) := by
  rw [Rat.lt_div_iff growth]
  unfold income
  grind

results.title: The material bound on justice
results.text: If everyone receives at least q times their needs and total access is at most Y, then q times total needs cannot exceed Y.
steps: Sum the individual lower bounds over the population.
Apply the aggregate resource constraint.
results.limit: The list must enumerate the population once for the population interpretation; the algebra holds for any list.

proof.code:
theorem maximin_resource_bound {P : Type} (people : List P) (needs access : P → Rat)
    (q Y : Rat) (lower : ∀ i, i ∈ people → q * needs i ≤ access i)
    (budget : total people access ≤ Y) : q * total people needs ≤ Y := by
  have hsum := total_monotone people (fun i => q * needs i) access lower
  have hlinear := total_linear people needs (fun _ => 0) q 0
  simp only [Rat.zero_mul, Rat.add_zero] at hlinear
  rw [hlinear] at hsum
  grind

results.title: An allocation attaining the bound
results.text: Every feasible lower satisfaction level is at most Y/B. Allocating (Y/B) times each person’s needs spends exactly Y and achieves that common ratio.
results.formula: Q* = Y / B ; cᵢ* = (Y / B)bᵢ ; B = Σ bᵢ > 0
steps: The resource bound implies q ≤ Y/B because B is positive.
The proportional allocation sums to (Y/B)B = Y; each needs ratio is Y/B.
results.limit: Requires divisible resources and fixed output. It does not prove that a real collective institution can implement this allocation.

proof.code:
theorem proportional_allocation_attains {P : Type} (people : List P)
    (needs access : P → Rat) (q Y : Rat)
    (needsPositive : ∀ i, 0 < needs i)
    (lower : ∀ i, i ∈ people → q * needs i ≤ access i)
    (budget : total people access ≤ Y) (positive : 0 < total people needs) :
    q ≤ Y / total people needs ∧
    total people (fun i => (Y / total people needs) * needs i) = Y ∧
    ∀ i, ((Y / total people needs) * needs i) / needs i = Y / total people needs := by
  have bound := maximin_resource_bound people needs access q Y lower budget
  have nz : total people needs ≠ 0 := by grind
  have lin := total_linear people needs (fun _ => 0) (Y / total people needs) 0
  simp only [Rat.zero_mul, Rat.add_zero] at lin
  constructor
  · apply Classical.byContradiction
    intro h
    have hlt : Y / total people needs < q := by grind
    have := (Rat.div_lt_iff positive).mp hlt
    grind
  · constructor
    · rw [lin]
      grind
    · intro i
      have hi : needs i ≠ 0 := by have := needsPositive i; grind
      grind

results.title: When collective access improves on private access
results.text: A nonowner is materially better off under equal collective allocation exactly when the collective/private output ratio exceeds the labor-and-redistribution share.
results.formula: cᶜᵢ > cᴾᵢ  ⇔  Yᶜ / Yᴾ > λ + τ(1 − λ)
steps: Insert zero ownership and equal labor income into the income formula.
Compare with Yᶜ/n and cancel the positive population and private output.
results.limit: A per-person comparison, not Pareto superiority. Needs coverage additionally requires Yᶜ ≥ Σbᵢ; majority application requires a majority of nonowners.

proof.code:
theorem collective_improvement_iff (privateOutput commonOutput laborShare tax n : Rat)
    (population : 0 < n) (production : 0 < privateOutput) :
    income (laborShare * privateOutput / n) 0
      ((1 - laborShare) * privateOutput) tax n < commonOutput / n ↔
    laborShare + tax * (1 - laborShare) < commonOutput / privateOutput := by
  have hn : n ≠ 0 := by grind
  have identity : income (laborShare * privateOutput / n) 0
      ((1 - laborShare) * privateOutput) tax n =
      ((laborShare + tax * (1 - laborShare)) * privateOutput) / n := by
    unfold income
    grind
  rw [identity, Rat.div_lt_iff population]
  have cancel : (commonOutput / n) * n = commonOutput := by grind
  rw [cancel, Rat.lt_div_iff production]

results.title: A strict majority wins a binary vote
results.text: If yes and no ballots sum to the electorate and yes exceeds half, yes exceeds no.
results.formula: yes + no = n ∧ 2yes > n ⇒ yes > no
steps: Substitute the total number of ballots and rearrange the integer inequality.
results.limit: Lean checks the vote count, not informed preferences, actual democratic institutions or implementation. Material advantage does not force a political preference.

proof.code:
theorem majority_choice (yes no n : Nat) (ballots : yes + no = n)
    (majority : n < 2 * yes) : MajorityWins yes no := by
  unfold MajorityWins
  omega

results.title: Private concentration need not be necessary
results.text: A sustainable innovating regime without concentrated private capital refutes the claim that such concentration is necessary for sustainable innovation.
steps: Apply the proposed necessity claim to the collective counterexample.
Its absence of private concentration contradicts that claim.
results.limit: A conditional logical result. The feasibility of that collective infrastructure remains an empirical and institutional question.

proof.code:
theorem collective_innovation_not_necessary {R : Type}
    (privateConcentration sustainableInnovation : R → Prop) (common : R)
    (innovation : sustainableInnovation common) (collective : ¬ privateConcentration common) :
    ¬ (∀ r, sustainableInnovation r → privateConcentration r) := by
  intro necessary
  exact collective (necessary common innovation)

results.title: The reduced principles have a model
results.text: A two-person, two-regime example satisfies the model: equal access is just and covers needs; the alternative deprives one person and is not just.
steps: Construct positive needs, nonnegative access and witnessed minima explicitly.
Check admissibility, maximin and essential coverage in the finite example.
results.limit: Liberties and democracy are true by construction in this abstract witness. This is no historical or institutional validation.

proof.code:
theorem reduced_principles_have_model :
    Just exampleModel true ∧ UniversalNeeds exampleModel true ∧ ¬ Just exampleModel false := by
  have good : Just exampleModel true := by
    refine ⟨⟨True.intro, True.intro, True.intro⟩, ?_⟩
    intro r _
    cases r <;> decide +kernel
  have needs : UniversalNeeds exampleModel true := by intro i; cases i <;> decide +kernel
  refine ⟨good, needs, ?_⟩
  apply avoidable_deprivation_not_just exampleModel false true good.1 needs
  exact ⟨false, by decide +kernel⟩

results.title: Twice the output, 90 people worse off
results.text: In the exact 100-person example, output increases from 100 to 200 while 90 people lose access and fall below the needs threshold of 0.75. Total essential needs are 75.
steps: Evaluate both allocations over all 100 individuals.
Sum resources and count the individuals who lose access or fall below 3/4.
results.limit: A kernel-checked counterexample to automatic shared prosperity, not a prediction of the actual economy.

proof.code:
theorem majority_loss_example :
    total (List.range 100) before = 100 ∧
    total (List.range 100) after = 200 ∧
    ((List.range 100).filter (fun i => after i < before i)).length = 90 ∧
    ((List.range 100).filter (fun i => after i < (3 / 4 : Rat))).length = 90 ∧
    total (List.range 100) (fun _ => (3 / 4 : Rat)) = 75 := by
  decide +kernel

results.title: Redistribution can repair the example
results.text: With output and ownership unchanged, redistributing 13/38 of capital income gives each nonowner exactly 0.75 in the automated example.
steps: Evaluate the nonowner income formula with the specified tax and profit pool.
results.limit: Shows that the exclusion result does not establish communism as the unique solution. Output responses to redistribution are outside this example.

proof.code:
theorem redistribution_repairs_example :
    income (1 / 10) 0 190 (13 / 38) 100 = (3 / 4 : Rat) := by
  decide +kernel

conflicts.title: A best regime cannot always be improved
conflicts.text: H3 supplies a strictly best admissible regime. H9 supplies a strictly better admissible alternative to that same regime. These premises cannot hold together in one model.
steps: Strict superiority makes the candidate a maximin regime.
Unlimited strict improvement excludes every maximin regime.
conflicts.limit: Deselect H3 or H9 to continue exploring a compatible set of premises. This check detects this known conflict; it is not a general consistency solver.

proof.code:
theorem strict_best_conflicts_with_improvement {P R : Type} (m : Model P R) (best : R)
    (admissible : Admissible m best)
    (strict : ∀ r, Admissible m r → r ≠ best → m.floor r < m.floor best)
    (improvement : ∀ r, Admissible m r →
      ∃ s, Admissible m s ∧ m.floor r < m.floor s) : False := by
  have bestJust := (unique_best_is_unique_just m best admissible strict).1
  exact no_maximum_no_just m improvement ⟨best, bestJust⟩
